sentences.ko: 그러게, 어쩌다 보니 포커 칠 줄 아는 여자를 아무도 몰라서 그래.
sentences.text: Yeah, we just don't happen to know any women that know how to play poker.

alts.text: We just don't know any girls who play poker, that's all.
As it happens, we are not acquainted with any women who know how to play poker.

sentences.note: **happen to**는 '어쩌다 보니 ~하다'라는 뜻이에요. 일부러 그런 게 아니라 사정이 그렇게 됐다고 할 때 씁니다. **don't happen to know**는 '마침 아는 사람이 없다'는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아니, 케이크를 망칠 거였으면 차라리 내가 구웠지.
sentences.text: All right, IF I WANTED THIS CAKE to be a disaster, I WOULD HAVE BAKED IT MYSELF.

alts.text: Seriously, I'd have just baked it myself if I wanted it ruined.
Had I wanted this cake to be a disaster, I would have baked it myself.

sentences.note: '그럴 거였으면 차라리 내가 했지'라고 남이 해 놓은 일에 투덜댈 때 쓰는 틀이에요. 본인 실력이 없다고 스스로 놀리는 농담이기도 해요. 핵심은 **would have baked it myself**처럼 'would have + 과거분사'로 이미 지난 일을 말하는 부분이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그러니까 노래하다가 중간에 내가 재채기해도 일부러 그런 거 아니야.
sentences.text: So if I sneeze in the middle of a song, it's not on purpose.

alts.text: Just so you know, if I sneeze mid-song, I don't mean it.
Should I sneeze during a song, please understand that it is not intentional.

sentences.note: **on purpose**는 '일부러'라는 뜻이에요. 미리 양해를 구하거나 해명할 때 'It's not on purpose'를 그대로 쓰면 돼요. **in the middle of**는 '~하는 도중에'라는 뜻으로 일상에서 아주 자주 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 나 어릴 때부터 발가락으로 25센트짜리 동전을 집을 수 있었어.
sentences.text: ever since I was little, I've been able to pick up quarters with my toes.

alts.text: I've always been able to grab coins with my toes, since I was a kid.
Since my childhood, I have been able to pick up quarters with my toes.

sentences.note: **ever since I was little**는 '어릴 때부터 쭉'이라는 뜻이에요. 자기만의 특기나 오래된 습관을 얘기할 때 딱 맞아요. 뒤에는 'I've been ~'처럼 현재완료가 따라옵니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 내가 이렇게 운이 좋다니, 진짜 믿기지가 않아.
sentences.text: And I can't believe how lucky I am.

alts.text: I'm so lucky, I seriously can't get over it.
I find it difficult to believe how fortunate I am.

sentences.note: **I can't believe how** 뒤에 형용사와 '주어 + 동사'를 붙이면 '이렇게 ~하다니 믿기지 않아'가 돼요. 감동하거나 놀랐을 때 씁니다. 'I'm very lucky'보다 감정이 훨씬 잘 실려요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 내일 뉴욕 가야 돼서 너무 싫은데, 그래도 아들 얼굴은 볼 수 있잖아. 우리 아들 너무 좋아.
sentences.text: I'm leaving for New York tomorrow, which I hate, but I get to see my son, who I love.

alts.text: Gotta fly to New York tomorrow. Hate it, but hey, I get to see my kid.
Tomorrow I will be travelling to New York, which I dislike, but I will have the chance to see my son, whom I love.

sentences.note: **which I hate** 처럼 말 중간에 내 기분을 툭 덧붙이면 한 문장으로 투덜거림과 반가움을 같이 전할 수 있어요. **I get to** 는 '~할 수 있게 되다'로, 좋은 기회가 생겼을 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.text: Why don't we just let the machine get that?

alts.text: Eh, just let it go to the machine.
Perhaps we could simply allow the answering machine to take the call.

sentences.note: 전화가 울리는데 받기 싫을 때 **let the machine get that** 이라고 해요. 요즘은 machine 자리에 voicemail 을 넣습니다. 초인종이나 전화가 울릴 때 '내가 받을게'도 I'll **get that** 이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: It's a- It's this cute little place on 10th Street.

alts.text: Cute little spot on 10th.
There is a charming little restaurant on 10th Street.

sentences.note: 상대가 모르는 가게를 처음 소개할 때 a 대신 this 를 써서 **this cute little place** 라고 하면 이야기하듯 생생하게 들려요. 형용사는 **cute little** 순서로 붙입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 음, 그게, 프랑스에 사는 친척 중에 그거 알 만한 사람이 있을지도 몰라.
sentences.text: Well, you know, I I may have relatives in France who would know.

alts.text: Hmm, maybe my family in France would know.
It is possible that some of my relatives in France could tell you.

sentences.note: '알 만한 사람이 있을지도 몰라'는 **I may have relatives** … **who would know** 처럼 사람 뒤에 who would know 를 붙여 말해요. 누구한테 물어보면 될지 떠올릴 때 쓰는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 걔네 지금 부엌에서 우리 먹을 거 챙기고 있어.
sentences.text: they're in the kitchen getting us something to eat.

alts.text: Oh, kitchen. Grabbing us some food.
At the moment, they are in the kitchen preparing something for us to eat.

sentences.note: **getting us something to eat** 은 '우리 먹을 거 갖다주는 중'이라는 뜻이에요. 누가 어디 갔냐고 물을 때 '부엌에서 ~하고 있어'처럼 장소 뒤에 -ing 를 바로 붙여 답하면 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends
